createpop.brewers_guide.section.overview: Create: Pop revolves around turning plain water into carbonated water, then combining that base with potions, sodas, dyes, or stabilizers in a Create mixer.
Every proper mix works in drink-sized portions of %s, so aim to feed the basin with at least that much of each fluid input.
Use this guide as a field manual: the
is where you keep your personal discoveries and tasting notes once you start experimenting.
createpop.brewers_guide.section.carb.lin: 1. Put water into a Create mixer basin.
3. Bottle, bucket, or pipe the result if you want to transport it before the next mix.
Carbonated water is the backbone for every first-generation soda. If a recipe feels like it should work but refuses to mix, check that you are starting from carbonated water instead of plain water.
createpop.brewers_guide.section.first_so: Turning any potion into a soda base
Mix carbonated water with almost any brewed
to create an experimental soda base. Negative brews, strong brews, and awkward-looking starts can all lead to very different outcomes.
The resulting soda carries its starting effects forward with drinkable timings and a color that helps identify it at a glance, so even a rough first mix can become the seed for something exceptional.
Once you have a base soda, you can remix it with other sodas, recolor it with
, or stabilize it if the recipe starts getting unruly. A tier-1 negative plus a tier-2 negative might still cascade into several positive results if the reaction breaks your way.
createpop.brewers_guide.section.rules.li: Mixing two different sodas combines their effects into a new drink. Matching effects tend to stack duration, while wildly uneven amounts lead to more dilution and shorter results.
lets you recolor an existing soda without changing its core effects, which is useful for theming batches or marking stronger blends.
You can also combine multiple dyes in succession; later recolors push the final shade more strongly than earlier ones.
Try to mix deliberately rather than randomly: once two inputs are the same exact soda, the mixer intentionally avoids wasting them on a pointless same-for-same combine.
createpop.brewers_guide.section.instabil: Every remix adds instability. The more complicated the drink becomes, the more likely it is to pick up drawbacks or otherwise drift away from the clean result you expected.
in a heated mixer to shave off about %s instability,

in a superheated mixer for about %s.
A little instability can be manageable, but if you are chasing polished recipes, stabilize between major remix steps instead of waiting until the very end.
An experienced brewer can even turn negative brews to their advantage: amethyst purification clears current instability and inverts harmful effects into beneficial ones.
createpop.brewers_guide.section.discover: is your long-term memory. Save learned recipes into it, reopen them later, and write down what made a batch good, bad, or worth revisiting.
When you discover something new, name it clearly and note what the drink felt like in practice: ingredients, effect mix, instability, taste theme, and whether it is worth mass production.
The best soda lab is iterative: discover a base, record it, refine it, and only then commit it to your regular production line.

advancement.createpop.root.title: Shake Well Before Consuming
advancement.createpop.root.description: Something fizzy this way comes, and the machine is humming along like it knows what's about to happen. You've made a choice, and that choice is carbonated.
advancement.createpop.guide_obtained.des: A guide with pages and diagrams that mostly make sense. Reading it is optional. Surviving without it is also optional, technically.
A blank notebook, intended for a professional working in a workshop near several rotating blades -- which means whatever you write in it is going to become evidence eventually, so try to keep the doodles tasteful.
advancement.createpop.soda_named.title: Say My Name
advancement.createpop.soda_named.descrip: You named it, you branded it, and whatever it does to the next consumer is now part of the legend you're quietly building one batch at a time.
advancement.createpop.carbonated_water_o: Are You Sure About That, Water?
You violently spun a diamond in water until it became spicy. The scientific community is appalled, but the mouthfeel is exceptional.
advancement.createpop.carbonated_water_c: It's water, allegedly, though your mouth has filed a formal complaint and the bubbles seem to have opinions on at least three unrelated subjects.
advancement.createpop.soda_obtained.titl: We're In The Soda Business Now
advancement.createpop.soda_obtained.desc: A potion, a basin, and a wheel spinning at unwise speeds -- somehow that combination produced a drink, and the drink is moving, and you've decided not to ask about the residue on the floor.
advancement.createpop.soda_consumed.desc: Every clinical trial needs a willing participant, and you volunteered before anyone could finish reading the waiver, which the control group will hear about whenever you hand them the next bottle.
advancement.createpop.soda_poured.title: Quality Control: Failed
advancement.createpop.soda_poured.descri: You tipped a carefully developed product onto the dirt and it destabilised on contact, leaving the floor to absorb the consequences as it has done many times before and will do many times again.
advancement.createpop.compound_soda_obta: Both sodas turned up to the party with their own status effects and refused to leave, and the resulting drink has the structural integrity of a hardmode invasion event happening inside one ribcage.
advancement.createpop.negative_soda_obta: The soda has developed character, specifically the kind of character that makes nearby pharmacists go quiet and start filling out forms. Instability was mentioned on page two in fairly bold text.
advancement.createpop.perfect_soda_obtai: Zero instability, every effect clean, every reading exactly where it should be -- the sort of purity that gets written up in journals nobody outside the lab will ever read.
advancement.createpop.stabilised_with_ac: You used a log in a heated machine to fix a drink, and the genuinely upsetting part is that this is roughly how it works in real life, which the patch notes have so far declined to explain.
advancement.createpop.stabilised_with_ma: It's hot, it's gooey, and it really shouldn't work, but the cream did its job without complaint and slid quietly back into the underworld like a reliable contractor between gigs.
advancement.createpop.stabilised_with_am: Superheated crystal inverted every negative into a positive, and somewhere in the distance a chemist is weeping while a geologist weeps for entirely unrelated reasons.
